subject: Dedicated pool jitter mitigation & throughput SLO spec — Chronos Analytics
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@chronos.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Timothy Ward <timothy.ward@chronos.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — token throughput spikes during peak 

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Chronos is excited about the latency profile we saw. Our infra team ran a 48h trial on the API and we noticed periodic throughput jitter during our afternoon peak (14:00–16:00 UTC): short ~10–30s windows where effective tokens/sec drops by ~30% and 99th-pct single-token latency spikes to ~300–400ms. That behavior is causing downstream batching backpressure in our ingestion pipeline.

We plan to move to a Reserved GPU pool (we're targeting 4x A100-equivalent GPUs) and need to understand:
- How Redwood quantifies and guarantees steady-state throughput for a reserved pool (tokens/sec per GPU or per pool)?
- What queueing behavior we should expect when headroom is exhausted (preemption, soft queueing, request rejection)?
- Options for an SLO or runbook we can include in the contract to cover brief jitter windows (e.g., credits, burst buffering, or automatic fallback to a smaller model variant).

I've attached a small CSV with our request profile (short_examples in chronos-throughput-profile.csv) and a draft SLA with the performance targets we want to discuss (requested-sla-draft.pdf). Can we get a short playbook from Redwood that maps servicing guarantees to the contract language?

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Chronos Analytics
alyssa.chen@chronos.ai
---
Attachments: chronos-throughput-profile.csv (text/csv), requested-sla-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@chronos.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — token throughput spikes during peak 

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the data and the clear ask. Looping in Ben (sales lead on Chronos) and Marissa (SRE / capacity planning) so we can propose a concrete mitigation playbook.

High-level notes from first pass:
- Short jitter windows like you describe often correlate with cross-tenant tail events and autoscaling/failover transitions in shared infra. With a Reserved pool we should eliminate noisy neighbors, but preemption and scheduling within the pool can still introduce short-lived contention (e.g., driver restarts, node maintenance).
- For 4x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs we typically characterize steady-state throughput as a tokens/sec range per GPU for a specific model + context length. We need to pin which model variant and average context length to give an exact number.
- We can offer a two-pronged contract approach: (1) deterministic throughput floor for sustained windows (e.g., 4 GPUs => X tokens/sec sustained for 10m windows at 95% availability) and (2) a short-jitter protection clause covering transient spikes with automatic mitigation (KV prefix caching, local burst queue, and temporary fallback to a slightly lower-cost/latency-optimized quantized variant).

Ben/Marissa — can you draft a playbook that maps the following items into contract language: guaranteed throughput floor, 99th-pct latency target for single-token generation, mitigation actions (cache bypass, local burst, model fallback), measurement windows, and credit/remediation policy for violations?

Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@chronos.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — Dedicated pool jitter mitigation & throughput SLO spec — Chronos Analytics

Hi Alyssa — appreciate the profile and for surfacing the production symptom. Quick proposal below (summary + ask):

Summary proposal (for 4x A100-equivalent reserved pool; assuming model: redwood-llm-1-large, avg context 2k tokens):
- Sustained throughput floor: 4 GPUs => nominal 18,000 tokens/sec aggregate (±10%) measured over 10-minute rolling windows. This is our "throughput floor" that we guarantee 99.5% of the time per calendar month.
- Latency SLO: 99th-percentile single-token generation latency <= 160ms for requests that fit the 2k context and use streaming.
- Short-jitter protection: For transient spikes (<60s) we will: 1) apply prefix (KV) caching for repeated prefixes, 2) route eligible requests to an in-pool local burst queue (up to 30s per request), 3) automatic model-fallback to redwood-llm-1-medium quantized variant if latency exceeds 220ms for >12s.
- Remediation: If the sustained throughput floor is missed for a rolling 30-minute window, Chronos is eligible for token credits proportional to the measured deficit (formula: credits = deficit_tokens / 10,000). For transient jitter events that are mitigated by automatic fallback we propose an urgent post-incident note and no credit unless mitigation failed to bring service within SLO within 2 minutes.

Open items / asks from Chronos:
1) Confirm the model variant + typical average prompt length/context distribution so we can produce an exact tokens/sec per GPU baseline.
2) Confirm whether you need preemption protection (zero preemption) or if soft preemption with graceful draining is acceptable. Zero preemption implies extra reserved capacity and a price uplift.
3) Procurement contact + preferred contract language trigger for credits and rolling measurement windows.

Next steps: Marissa will prepare an operations playbook (runbook + measurement queries for metrics) and a concise contract paragraph you can drop into your draft SLA. Once we have model/context confirmation we will bench and return GPU tokens/sec numbers for the pool.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@chronos.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool jitter mitigation & throughput SLO spec — Chronos Analytics

Thanks — this is very helpful and close to what we had in mind. A few clarifications:
- Confirmed model: redwood-llm-1-large for production inference; average context across our traffic is ~1,800 tokens (95th pct < 3k).
- Preemption: zero preemption during our primary window (12:00–20:00 UTC) is a hard requirement; outside that window soft preemption is acceptable. If zero preemption is a paid add-on we need the delta price.
- We accept the proposed transient protection stack, but would like a stricter fallback threshold: please make automatic model-fallback trigger at 180ms for >10s (we want to avoid visible user impact).
- Procurement contact: procurement@chronos.ai (tim will lead). Please include a sample contract paragraph for both the throughput floor and the transient jitter remediation so legal can review.

Would you also propose a 48h canary schedule and an observability checklist we can run during the canary? We'd prefer to start the canary next Tuesday (24 Nov) if that works.

Best,
Alyssa

2) Ben / I will draft two short contract paragraphs: (a) throughput floor (18k tokens/sec aggregate example will be adjusted after benching for your context), (b) transient jitter remediation & credit calculation (we'll update fallback threshold to 180ms >10s per your ask).
3) We can start the 48h canary on Tue 24 Nov. Proposed plan: 24–26 Nov, 14:00–18:00 UTC daily stress windows included, daily check-ins at 18:30 UTC with your infra team. We will run bench tests on Mon 23 Nov to finalize the tokens/sec per GPU number.
